findings.title: Write lock held across file and network I/O
findings.body: In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets acquires entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() and then does readWebAssetsFromFile and readWebAssetsFromCDN while still holding it (defer Unlock). A write lock on a sync.RWMutex blocks all RLock readers, so every concurrent cache hit that should take the fast RLock path at the top of the function will block for the duration of the file read or HTTP fetch. The consequence is unnecessary serialization, latency spikes and thread pile-up under load. Load outside the lock (with double-check/singleflight) and only hold the lock to publish the result.

findings.title: Shared mutable cached pointer returned without copy
findings.body: In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets caches a *dtos.EntryPointAssets in a global and returns the same pointer to all callers on the fast path. The mutex only protects the global pointer itself, not the pointed-to struct/slices. Anyone reading only this finding should understand: if any caller mutates the returned object (for example calling SetContentDeliveryURL or appending to JSFiles), those writes race with concurrent readers of the same shared object and the race detector will still fire despite the new mutex. The consequence is a remaining data race / cross-request corruption. Fix by treating the cached value as immutable, returning a deep copy, or documenting and enforcing no mutation by callers.
